cf.title: Adding a stored generated column without long-lived locks

input.subject: Adding a stored generated column without long-lived locks

verdict_reasoning: The goal has support in the thread and no objection to it survived. The design is not settled. replication-ondisk-1 describes a path where clearing attmissingval without a rewrite turns existing values into NULL. standards-compat-2 shows the required constraint shape depends on an uncommitted function, with the fallback left open in message #42. The proof rule has changed three times, so the list should agree on it before code review.

brief.title: Turn a backfilled column into a stored generated column without rewrite
brief.problem: Adding a stored generated column to a large table today rewrites the table under an AccessExclusiveLock. The author hit this in production and wants a way for operators to do this migration online.
brief.proposed_design: A new ALTER TABLE subcommand turns a regular column into a stored generated column, taking the generation expression from a named, valid check constraint and never rewriting or scanning the table. The user first adds the column, a trigger, and a NOT VALID constraint, backfills, then runs VALIDATE. v12 requires the constraint to be CHECK (pg_datum_image_equal(col, expr)), a new function from a separate patch that compares binary images.
user_visible_surface: New syntax: alter table ... alter column col add generated using constraint constr_name stored.
New SQL function pg_datum_image_equal(anyelement, anyelement) returns boolean, from Matthias van de Meent's separate patch, included as v12-0001.
The command fails on identity, serial, already generated, partition key, foreign key with actions, and foreign table columns.
On partitioned or inheritance tables the command works only on the root without ONLY.
psql tab completion for the new syntax, and a new injection point that detects table scans and rewrites.
author_claims: The command fills a gap next to SET EXPRESSION and DROP EXPRESSION, as the reverse of DROP EXPRESSION.
With a valid pg_datum_image_equal constraint, stored values match what the expression would produce, so later rewrites and pg_dump/pg_restore do not fail.
Both = and IS NOT DISTINCT FROM are unsound: NULL results and values equal by = but with different images, like numeric 1.0 and 1.00, break consistency.
A reviewer saw the relation file stay unchanged on a 1,000,000-row table.
Logical replication works if the subscriber is prepared with triggers when generated columns are not published.
brief.thread_state: Laurenz Albe reviewed through v10 and marked it Ready for Committer, but the author withdrew that after finding the IS NOT DISTINCT FROM flaw; Álvaro Herrera questioned whether it matters and Matthias van de Meent said it does. v12 now depends on the uncommitted pg_datum_image_equal patch, and no one has replied to it yet.
unclear: What happens to this patch if the pg_datum_image_equal patch is not committed, beyond falling back to ROW()::record *= ROW()::record.
Whether every type, including extension types like PostGIS geometry, can be backfilled so that it passes the binary image check.
Which lock the command takes and for how long, beyond avoiding the table rewrite.
Whether the leftover constraint, which the command no longer drops, interacts with later SET EXPRESSION or DROP EXPRESSION.
No committer has given a view on the syntax or the SQL standard conflict risk raised by Laurenz Albe.
search_queries: alter table generated always as stored

objections.title: Clearing attmissingval can turn unrewritten tuples to NULL
objections.failure_scenario: An operator runs `alter table t add column c int not null default 0`, which uses a fast default with no rewrite. The backfill updates only rows `where c is distinct from expr`, VALIDATE passes, and the conversion clears attmissingval. Old tuples whose expr is 0 were never updated, so they now read NULL in a not-null column.
objections.argument: Message #42 says v12 clears atthasmissing and attmissingval for consistency with CREATE TABLE, and the command does no scan or rewrite. For tuples written before the ADD COLUMN, attmissingval is the only source of the column value. The proposal does not say why every tuple must physically hold the column before the catalog entry is removed. A batched, idempotent backfill that skips unchanged rows is a common pattern.
objections.author_must_show: What guarantees that no tuple still depends on attmissingval when it is cleared, or does the command refuse when atthasmissing is set?

critic.reasoning: SET EXPRESSION and ALTER COLUMN TYPE clear the missing value because they rewrite the table, and this command does not rewrite. Message #42 does not say what guarantees that no tuple still reads its value from attmissingval.

objections.title: DDL contract depends on an uncommitted function recognized by shape
objections.failure_scenario: Operators write migration runbooks against the documented form CHECK (pg_datum_image_equal(col, expr)). If the separate patch lands under another name, with other NULL semantics, or does not land, the documented form changes. In the ROW()::record *= fallback, every runbook written against the earlier form then fails with "not of the form".
objections.argument: In v12 the user-facing contract of the command is a literal function call inside a CHECK constraint, and that function comes from v12-0001, which has its own review (message #42). In message #42 the fallback is left open. Existing proof shortcuts such as SET NOT NULL and ATTACH PARTITION rely on constraint semantics. They do not match a specific function name, so this would be a new mechanism, and the material does not yet justify it.
objections.author_must_show: Is the pg_datum_image_equal shape a contract Postgres can keep across releases, and what is the accepted form if that function is not committed as proposed?

critic.reasoning: The runbook scenario is weak because no release has shipped the documented form. The dependency is real: v12 cannot be committed before v12-0001, and message #42 leaves the fallback constraint shape open.

objections.title: Constraint left behind after conversion conflicts with later SET EXPRESSION
objections.failure_scenario: An operator converts column b using CHECK (pg_datum_image_equal(b, a * 2)) and keeps the constraint, as v12 now does. Months later someone runs SET EXPRESSION AS (a * 3). The table rewrite checks the old constraint, which fails on every row, and the error names a constraint the operator no longer remembers.
objections.argument: Following message #8 and message #12, v12 no longer drops the constraint, citing SET NOT NULL and ATTACH PARTITION. In those cases the leftover constraint stays true after any later change to the column. Here it duplicates the generation expression, so the two can drift apart through SET EXPRESSION or DROP EXPRESSION. The documentation hunk does not say what to do with the constraint afterwards, and it does not mention this interaction.
objections.author_must_show: What happens to the leftover constraint under SET EXPRESSION, DROP EXPRESSION and pg_dump, and why should it stay instead of being dropped or documented as removable?

critic.reasoning: v12 keeps the constraint and the documentation hunk does not say what to do with it afterwards. A later SET EXPRESSION with a different expression would fail the rewrite on that constraint, and the brief lists this interaction as open.

objections.title: Subscribers silently stop receiving the converted column
objections.failure_scenario: A publication uses the default, which does not publish generated columns. The column reaches the subscriber during the backfill. After the conversion runs on the publisher, new and updated rows arrive without it, and the subscriber column keeps NULL or its default. Nobody sees an error, so the drift shows up later in reports or after a failover to the subscriber.
objections.argument: Message #10 describes this hazard and a workaround with triggers on the subscriber, but the TAP tests were left out. The alter_table.sgml hunk in v12 does not mention logical replication. With ADD COLUMN the column is new on both sides. Here the column changes from replicated to not replicated in the middle of a migration that operators run online.
objections.author_must_show: Will the documentation and tests cover the procedure for subscribers when generated columns are not published, or will the command warn when the table is in such a publication?

critic.reasoning: Message #10 describes the hazard and a workaround with subscriber triggers, but the v12 documentation hunk does not mention replication. An operator who follows the documented recipe would not learn of it.

objections.title: Restriction list must mirror every generated-column rule by hand
objections.failure_scenario: A later release adds a new rule that CREATE TABLE and ADD COLUMN enforce for stored generated columns. The new conversion path is not updated, so a user converts a column into a state that CREATE TABLE would reject. They find out when pg_dump output fails to restore.
objections.argument: The command reaches a catalog state through a second path, guarded by its own list of exclusions: identity, serial, partition key, FK actions, foreign tables, references to other generated columns. Message #42 adds two of these (FK actions, atthasmissing) after the patch had been marked Ready for Committer, which shows the list drifts. The proposal does not say whether these checks are shared with the CREATE TABLE code or copied, or what fails if a future rule is missed.
objections.author_must_show: Are the eligibility checks shared with the CREATE TABLE and ADD COLUMN code, so that a new generated-column restriction applies here without anyone changing this command?

critic.reasoning: Message #42 added the FK-action and foreign-table restrictions after the patch was marked Ready for Committer, so the list has already missed rules. The material does not say whether the checks are shared with the CREATE TABLE path.

refuted.title: Logical replication silently stops carrying the column's values
refuted.failure_scenario: A publication uses the default and does not publish generated columns, and the subscriber has a regular column b filled by replicated changes. After the conversion on the publisher, new inserts and updates arrive without b. The subscriber stores NULL, and nobody sees an error until someone queries the subscriber.
refuted.argument: In message #10 the author describes this change in behaviour and asks users to add triggers on the subscriber first. The documentation hunk for ALTER TABLE does not mention replication. A user who follows the documented recipe on a publisher therefore loses data on the subscriber without warning.
refuted.author_must_show: Where will the documentation warn about subscribers, and should the command at least warn when the table is in a publication that does not publish generated columns?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-2, which states the subscriber outcome more exactly and also notes that the TAP tests were left out.

refuted.title: Soundness rests on an uncommitted function with no committer view
refuted.failure_scenario: The syntax ships tied to CHECK (pg_datum_image_equal(col, expr)). Later the meaning of that function changes, or the project falls back to ROW()::record *= ROW()::record. The documented constraint shape then changes after release, and users' migration scripts stop matching the required shape.
refuted.argument: The correctness rule changed three times: from = (message #25), to IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (message #30), to image equality (message #42). Each flaw was found after a reviewer had signed off. v12 depends on a separate patch that nobody has reviewed in this thread. The only committer who commented (message #33) questioned whether the binary-image problem matters. No committer has said they would own the proof that a valid constraint guarantees the stored values match the expression.
refuted.author_must_show: Which committer has accepted pg_datum_image_equal as the permanent contract, and is the command still sound if that function's semantics differ for detoasted or expanded values?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2 on the dependency and the fallback. The remaining point about committer ownership belongs in the committability field, and a committer, Álvaro Herrera, is a registered reviewer.

refuted.title: Virtual generated columns or trigger-maintained columns may already cover the need
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator who needs the column online can run `alter table t add column c ... generated always as (expr) virtual`, which does not rewrite the table, and can build `create index concurrently` on expr if lookups are needed. Another option is the trigger and valid check constraint that the proposal's own procedure already sets up. If those cover most cases, the project carries new syntax and a new ALTER TABLE path that only makes existing results more convenient.
refuted.argument: Message #1 states the need as having no way to add a stored generated column without a rewrite. No message compares this with virtual generated columns or with keeping the trigger plus constraint as the final state. The operator must build that same trigger and constraint anyway (messages #1, #10). The new command then mainly relabels the column as GENERATED, so a committer would likely ask which concrete case virtual columns or that end state cannot serve.
refuted.author_must_show: Which workloads need a stored generated column, rather than a virtual one or a trigger-maintained column with the check constraint, and why do those alternatives fail there?

critic.reasoning: Virtual columns recompute the expression on every read and do not allow user-defined functions or types, so they do not serve cases like the tsvector column in message #37. Laurenz Albe, Álvaro Herrera and conference attendees (messages #5, #6) independently recognized the need.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: The command trusts existing heap values without a scan and clears attmissingval without a rewrite.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The converted column stops being sent to subscribers when the publication does not publish generated columns.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: v12-0001 adds a pg_proc entry, and the command changes pg_attribute and pg_attrdef for the column.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes parsenodes.h for the new ALTER TABLE subcommand, which extensions that inspect utility statements see.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: New non-standard syntax ADD GENERATED USING CONSTRAINT ... STORED; message #5 raised a possible future conflict with the standard.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: Restore recomputes the column from the expression, and the leftover check constraint is dumped with the table.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: The patch adds psql tab completion for the new syntax.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A second path to the generated-column catalog state carries its own restriction list and a constraint matched by function name.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: What guarantees that no tuple still reads its value from attmissingval when the command clears it, or does the command refuse when atthasmissing is set?
What constraint shape does the command accept if pg_datum_image_equal is not committed as proposed, and can Postgres keep that shape across releases?
What happens to the leftover constraint under a later SET EXPRESSION or DROP EXPRESSION, and why keep it after the conversion?
Will the documentation or the command warn when the table is in a publication that does not publish generated columns?
Are the eligibility checks shared with the CREATE TABLE and ADD COLUMN code, or copied into this command?

committability.owner_note: Álvaro Herrera is a registered reviewer and commented in message #33, but has not replied to v12 or given a view on the syntax. The owner needs to know ALTER TABLE, generated columns and fast defaults.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the claim that a valid constraint proves the stored values match the expression, with no scan to catch a mistake. The syntax and the required constraint shape are permanent once released.
committability.author_follow_up: The author has posted twelve versions since March 2026 and withdrew the Ready for Committer status after finding a soundness flaw in the patch.

priority.reason: Operators of large tables need this, and reviewers and conference attendees confirmed the need. The main patch is about 74 KB in tablecmds.c and gram.y and depends on a separate uncommitted function, and the soundness rule changed again in v12.

provisional_note: Without the code I could not check how v12 handles atthasmissing, which lock the command takes, or whether the eligibility checks are shared with CREATE TABLE. Only 3 of the 42 messages were visible, so later messages are known only through the objections.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: DOCS for generated column replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: Peter Smith proposed an "Examples" subsection for the new "Generated Column Replication" documentation page. The patch adds a few self-contained publication and subscription examples, including one showing that a publication column list overrides publish_generated_columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila judged the current text and example sufficient, and preferred to wait for user feedback on the new feature before adding more examples. No one else supported the patch, so vignesh C closed the entry for lack of interest, open to revisit if users ask for it.

This is a new feature, and I think it is better to
get some feedback from users. We can add more examples or information
based on real user feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: COPY WHERE clause generated/system column reference
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patches make COPY FROM ... WHERE work with generated columns: they expand virtual generated columns in the WHERE clause and compute stored generated columns before the WHERE clause is checked. They also reject system columns other than tableoid in the WHERE clause.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed a smaller fix that rejects generated columns in COPY FROM WHERE with a clear error, and left tableoid for a separate thread. He then argued that support should not be added, because generated columns belong to the target table while the WHERE clause filters input data. Masahiko Sawada had shown that computing stored generated columns before the WHERE clause runs them before BEFORE INSERT triggers, so the WHERE clause changes the row the trigger sees.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This seems fundamentally wrong, because generated columns are a
property of the target table, but the COPY WHERE clause is meant to
filter the input data.

precedents_retrieved.title: generated columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: Peter Eisentraut proposed implementing SQL-standard generated columns (GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr)), with the generation expression stored in pg_attrdef like a default and MySQL/Oracle-style VIRTUAL|STORED syntax. Only the VIRTUAL (computed-on-read) variant was fully implemented; STORED, various ALTER TABLE forms and index support were deferred.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review by Jaime Casanova found multiple bugs: generated columns showed no value through a view, inheritance produced a malformed default and a server crash on insert, ALTER COLUMN TYPE on the referenced or generated column failed with internal errors, triggers saw NULL for the generated column, and the generation expression could be dropped via DROP DEFAULT. Based on these reviews, the commitfest manager marked the entry Returned with feedback, asking for an updated version to be resubmitted.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Based on this review, and the errors noted in upthread in the previous review,
I’m marking this Returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical decoding to output generated columns
precedents_retrieved.authors: Peter Smith (smithpb2250), Shubham Khanna (skhanna), Shlok Kyal (shlokkyal)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let pgoutput send generated column values in logical replication, so consumers get a complete row instead of computing generated columns on the subscriber. The work added replication of generated columns named in a publication column list, then a publish_generated_columns publication parameter.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Most of the work was committed before the entry closed: generated columns in column lists and the publish_generated_columns parameter. After that commit, Peter Eisentraut asked how the feature should work with the proposed virtual generated columns, which he thought could not be replicated, and Amit Kapila suggested limiting the option to stored generated columns. The thread then went idle in Waiting on Author, and Michael Paquier returned the entry until that question is settled.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As of now this thread is just waiting on author and idle in the CF app for no real purpose.

precedents_retrieved.title: Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
Reverted commit(s): Revert to 9.6 treatment of ALTER TYPE enumtype ADD VALUE.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Originally committed as 15bc038f (plus some follow-ups), this was
reverted in 28e07270 due to a problem discovered in parallel
workers.  This new version corrects that problem by sending the
list of uncommitted enum values to parallel workers.

Here follows the original commit message describing the change:

To prevent possibly breaking indexes on enum columns, we must keep
uncommitted enum values from getting stored in tables, unless we
can be sure that any such column is new in the current transaction.

Formerly, we enforced this by disallowing ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE
from being executed at all in a transaction block, unless the target
enum type had been created in the current transaction.  This patch
removes that restriction, and instead insists that an uncommitted enum
value can't be referenced unless it belongs to an enum type created
in the same transaction as the value.  Per discussion, this should be
a bit less onerous.  It does require each function that could possibly
return a new enum value to SQL operations to check this restriction,
but there aren't so many of those that this seems unmaintainable.

precedents_retrieved.title: CHECK constraint deferrable Support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets CHECK constraints be declared DEFERRABLE and INITIALLY DEFERRED, as the SQL standard allows, so SET CONSTRAINTS can delay a CHECK until commit. Rows that fail a deferrable CHECK are rechecked at commit time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the CHECK implementation assumes constraints are immutable, and the patch does not change that assumption, so he called the feature a toy. Others then argued it should be dropped or combined with deferrable NOT NULL, which Robert Haas and Vik Fearing disputed. Dean Rasheed also reported open bugs, including a deferred constraint that still failed immediately and a wrong constraint-exclusion result. The visible messages do not show why the author withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I continue to assert that basing this feature on the current CHECK implementation will produce nothing but a toy feature, that's not only of little practical use but will be an active foot-gun for people who expect it to do more than it can.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
A view defined as "select <something> where false" had the curious property
that the system wouldn't check whether users had the privileges necessary
to select from it.  More generally, permissions checks could be skipped
for tables referenced in sub-selects or views that were proven empty by
constraint exclusion (although some quick testing suggests this seldom
happens in cases of practical interest).  This happened because the planner
failed to include rangetable entries for such tables in the finished plan.

views, but actually the issue is quite unrelated to matviews.  Therefore,
revert commit 200ba1667b3a8d7a9d559d2f05f83d209c9d8267 in favor of a more

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found, and the thread cites no earlier attempt at this idea. Message #2 points to the DROP EXPRESSION inheritance discussion and message #32 to the separate pg_datum_image_equal patch, but both are related work, not earlier rejections.

The thread raised a possible future conflict between this syntax and the SQL standard (message #5). Laurenz Albe accepted the syntax, so it is not raised here, but no committer has given a view on it yet.
The change is catalog-only: pg_attribute, pg_attrdef and the leftover constraint. It adds no WAL record and no wire protocol change. The dump and restore path is covered by the image equality check.

The proposal adds no new privilege or exposure. Only the table owner can run the new ALTER TABLE subcommand, and that owner can already add the same stored generated column with a rewrite. The generation expression must be immutable and comes from a CHECK constraint that is already valid on the owner's table. pg_datum_image_equal() compares only values the caller can already read, and NULL handling no longer lets concurrent writers slip rows past the check (message #25). Without the code I cannot check whether pg_datum_image_equal() is marked leakproof, and if it is, whether it can raise errors that depend on the data.
There is no hot-path cost for non-users: the command only runs when invoked, and the leftover constraint can be dropped by the user.
No contrib module or external tool turns a column into a generated column without a rewrite. The only existing alternatives are the in-core ones named above.

The material shows enough demand: the author hit the problem in production (message #1), several pgconf.dev attendees called it a real operational pain point (message #6), and Laurenz Albe and Álvaro Herrera accepted the use case. Costs fall mostly on users of the new subcommand. The dependency on pg_datum_image_equal and the syntax are design questions for other angles.
